frozen_rule_spec.selection_rationale: Rule B (max-Jaccard, single threshold) selected over A (R_old alone) and D (Dice alone) because it reaches FPR=0 (zero cross-episode unrelated-flock acceptances) at a lower/earlier threshold (0.25-0.30) than A (needs ~0.65) while matching D closely, giving Rule B the widest stable FPR=0 plateau (threshold in [0.25, 0.80]) of the three single-parameter rules at comparable TPR. Rule C (two-sided R_old/R_new) does not separate the calibration distributions any more cleanly than Rule B despite needing two parameters (best C: J=0.9896 at R_old>=0.4,R_new>=0.2, vs Rule B: J=0.9896 at a single threshold=0.20, J=0.9878 at threshold=0.30) -- the extra parameter buys no calibration-data benefit, so the simpler single-parameter rule is preferred per the task instruction to prefer the simplest robust rule. Threshold=0.30 (not the argmax-J value of 0.20-0.25) is chosen deliberately inside the wide, flat FPR=0 plateau (0.25-0.80) rather than at its edge, for stability against small calibration-sample resampling variance -- NOT chosen by looking at seeds 500-504. Coincidentally equals v1 LineageTracker611.RETENTION_MIN (lineage_611.py:39) -- noted as a sanity cross-check on scale, not as the reason for the choice (this calibration never reads that constant).
